reader.requirement: At --std 85, with WITH DUPLICATES IN ORDER, records whose keys all compare equal (relation-condition rules under the SORT's collating sequence) must be returned in the order of the USING files as written in the SORT statement (1985 allows several) and, within one file, in the order the records are accessed from it (relative slot order, indexed prime-key order), or in RELEASE order for an input procedure - for fixed and variable-length records, in memory or spilled.

edition-consulted.switches: construct table-sort-2002: a Format 2 (table) SORT, DUPLICATES included, is refused at 85 (COBOL0870), accepted at 2023

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the file SORT: the stable sort (index sort with release-order tie break, strict earliest-run merge) is unconditional and edition-blind; the table-SORT form exists only from 2002
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb704_85 covers an input procedure releasing six records in memory; not exercised: several USING files of each organization with access order differing from write order, ties from the COLLATING SEQUENCE (ALSO), variable-length records, and runs spilled to disk

probes.expected: USING F3(indexed, written T3,T1,T2) F4(empty) F1(seq) F2(relative, slots written 3,1,2) with ALSO ties: file order F3,F1,F2, each in access order (key order / slot order)

probes.expected: 3000 RELEASEs of a RECORD VARYING 5..9 SD, keys B/A/C interleaved: three groups A,B,C, each strictly in release order

reader.notes: The DUPLICATES flag is passed to CobolSort.Sort for traceability only; stability is unconditional, which satisfies GR3 and refines GR4's undefined order. USING files are released file by file in statement order through as-if READ NEXT, so access order is the file's own.
